displayedInputs.question: The data 1, 2, 3, 4 are arranged in ascending order, and \(n=4\). Find the 50th percentile. Rule: \(i=n\times 50\%\); when \(i\) is an integer, take the mean of the values at positions \(i\) and \(i+1\).
The data 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 are already ordered, and \(n=5\). Find the 20th percentile. If \(i=n\times 20\%\) is an integer, take the mean of the values at positions \(i\) and \(i+1\).
The data 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 are already ordered, and \(n=5\). Find the 50th percentile. Since \(i=2.5\) is not an integer, take the value at the next integer position, which is the 3rd position.
What does a percentile describe?

choices.B: A value at a certain percentage position in the sample

displayedInputs.question: What is the mean of the sample 2, 4, 6, 8?
What is the median of the sample 1, 3, 3, 7?
What is the mean of the sample 1, 2, 9?
When the data contain a particularly large value, which is often more robust for estimating the population center?
What is the range of the data 2, 4, 4, 6?
What is the variance of the data 2, 4, 4, 6? Calculate by dividing by \(n\).
What is the variance of the data 5, 5, 5? Calculate by dividing by \(n\).
What does a larger variance indicate?
Which is more suitable for showing the percentage each part represents of the whole?

choices.C: No need for a stem-and-leaf plot; use a pie chart here

displayedInputs.question: Which is more suitable for showing changes in daily temperature over a month?

choices.B: A single bar showing only the total

displayedInputs.question: The percentages of three categories in a pie chart are 20, 30, 50. What is their sum?
What should be used to compare the distribution of data across several contiguous intervals?
The weight data for 4 people in Group A are 60, 62, 64, 66. What is the mean?
What is the mean of Group B's data 70, 70, 70?
Group A has data 60, 62, 64, 66, and Group B has data 70, 70, 70. What is the mean of Group B minus the mean of Group A?
How should conclusions drawn from a sample in a case study be used?

choices.A: Treat them as exact values for the entire population
choices.B: Use them as estimates and explain how the sample was selected
choices.C: The sample size is no longer needed
choices.D: The data can be changed to make the conclusions look better

displayedInputs.question: A fair coin is tossed 2 times. How many sample points are there?
A bag contains 3 distinct balls, and 1 ball is drawn. How many sample points are there?
What is a sample space?

choices.A: It contains only the most likely outcome
choices.B: The set of all sample points
choices.D: The outcome that has already occurred

displayedInputs.question: Representing a sample space as a set relies on what?

choices.B: Using only roster notation and not set-builder notation
choices.D: There cannot be an empty set

displayedInputs.question: What is the probability of a certain event?
Which set corresponds to an impossible event?

choices.C: A set containing only one sample point

displayedInputs.question: A sample space has 5 sample points, and an event contains 5 of them. What is the probability of this event under the classical probability model?
What is a random event?

choices.A: An event that is certain to occur
choices.C: An object outside the sample space
choices.D: An event that may or may not occur

displayedInputs.question: A sample space has 8 sample points, and event \(A\) contains 3 of them. How many sample points does the complement of \(A\) contain?
\(A\) contains 4 sample points, \(B\) contains 5, and \(A\cap B\) contains 2. How many sample points does \(A\cup B\) contain?
What does \(A\cap B\) represent?

choices.A: At least one of \(A\) or \(B\) occurs

displayedInputs.question: Besides being mutually exclusive, what must complementary events satisfy?

choices.A: Their union is the entire sample space
choices.D: Each can contain only one sample point

displayedInputs.question: A bag contains 5 red balls and 3 blue balls, for a total of 8 balls. If 2 balls are drawn at random, what is the probability of drawing 2 red balls?
A fair die is rolled. What is the probability that the number rolled is greater than 4?
One number is selected from 1, 2, 3, 4, with each equally likely. What is the probability of selecting an even number?
What does the classical probability model require of the sample points?

choices.B: There are finitely many, and each is equally likely
choices.D: They must form a continuous interval

displayedInputs.question: \(A\) and \(B\) are mutually exclusive, with \(P(A)=1/4\) and \(P(B)=1/5\). What is \(P(A\cup B)\)?
The complement of an event has probability \(1/5\). What is the probability of the original event?
Why can the probabilities of mutually exclusive events be added directly?

choices.C: They cannot occur simultaneously, and their intersection is empty
choices.D: There are infinitely many sample points
